screening_results.reason: This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between PTSD patients and trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls (DSM-IV, CAPS reported). It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (non-PTSD > PTSD) with coordinates and cluster-level correction, and significant decreases in hippocampus and calcarine cortex. Results are provided as peak coordinates (table). Controls are trauma-exposed survivors without PTSD. Thus it meets I3 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I4 (whole-brain voxel-wise between-group GM contrast), I5 (coordinates/tables acceptable), and I6 (appropriate control group). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not longitudinal/treatment-only, not within-group-only, and reports significant between-group differences). Full text is sufficiently represented.

The study is an empirical English-language VBM MRI study comparing gray matter density between PTSD patients (n=12) and matched trauma-exposed controls (n=12). It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (PTSD < control) with reported peak coordinates/tables and a voxel-level threshold, and uses appropriate covariates. Controls are trauma-exposed non-PTSD subjects. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise within-group associations between gray matter volume and deployment/post-deployment measures in a sample of OEF/OIF veterans (n=29–32) with PTSD symptoms, but it does not report any voxel-wise between-group contrasts comparing PTSD patients versus control subjects. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls) and I4 (must report at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group PTSD vs control contrast). Exclusion criterion E8 (studies reporting only within-group results in PTSD patients without a qualifying between-group contrast) applies. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4.

This voxel-based morphometry MRI study reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts comparing PTSD patients (n=9) to trauma-exposed controls without PTSD (n=16), and identifies a significant gray-matter volume reduction in left anterior cingulate cortex (peak reported). The paper is empirical, in English, addresses GM volume differences in PTSD, and reports whole-brain results (with reported peaks and corrected inference), satisfying the meta-analysis objective. Control group is trauma-exposed without PTSD, which is an acceptable control population. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes a qualifying between-group contrast, and reports significant between-group differences).

This PLoS One study reports empirical structural MRI morphometry comparing gray matter volume between recent-onset PTSD patients and controls. It includes at least one whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls (Analysis 23155380_analysis_0: Normal control > Recent onset PTSD; FWE-corrected within whole brain) with reported peak coordinates in tables. Results pertain to GM volume and are presented for whole-brain analyses; control groups include both healthy and trauma-exposed non-PTSD participants. The study is cross-sectional (observational cohorts), not ROI-only, not a review, and reports significant between-group findings. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for morphometry studies of structural alterations associated with PTSD.

This study reports empirical, English-language structural MRI morphometry comparing PTSD patients with healthy controls using whole-brain analysis. NeuroStore extraction indicates a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast (controls > PTSD) with reported peak coordinates (3 peaks), gray matter density measure, two-sample t-test model, and corrected inference. Thus it satisfies inclusion I3 (empirical MRI GM volume comparison), I4 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I5 (results reported as coordinates/peaks), and I6 (healthy control population). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not a treatment/longitudinal-only study, and reports significant between-group differences). Full text appears available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry that compares gray matter volume between PTSD patients (cancer-related PTSD) and control groups. The NeuroStore record lists whole-brain spatial scope and reports between-group voxel-wise contrasts (cancer survivors with PTSD vs cancer survivors without PTSD and vs healthy subjects) with reported peaks. Control groups include both trauma-exposed (cancer survivors without PTSD) and healthy controls. Although small-volume correction (SVC) is reported for the orbitofrontal cortex, the extraction indicates whole-brain voxel-wise analyses were performed, so the study is not ROI-only. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical structural MRI study (I3) in English with an appropriate control group (I6) and reports voxel peaks and figures/tables (I5). However, the NeuroStore record shows only within-group correlations and condition-by-covariate interaction analyses (correlations between left amygdala volume and ACC/left amygdala GM density) and ROI manual tracing results for amygdala volume; it does not report a direct whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls comparing GM volume as required by I4. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E8 (reports only within-group/interaction results without a qualifying between-group GM voxel-wise contrast).

This is an empirical structural MRI morphometry study comparing pediatric PTSD patients (n=24) with age- and gender-matched controls using both volumetric and voxel-based morphometry. The NeuroStore record documents a whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrast (PTSD > control) for gray matter density with reported significant peaks (voxel-wise inference p<0.01 with cluster extent). Participants were assessed for PTSD (DSM-IV, CAPS-CA) and controls are healthy, meeting allowable control types. Results report significant GM differences (increased ventral PFC density and other regional differences). All required inclusion criteria for the review are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (whole-brain results are reported), not non-empirical, measures PTSD diagnosis, and includes between-group contrasts with significant findings. The study document appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports an empirical, English-language structural MRI morphometry comparison of gray matter volume between PTSD patients and controls (I3). It includes at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast (Controls > PTSD) with coordinates and FDR-corrected voxel-level inference (I4). Results are reported as peaks in a table (coordinates), satisfying that qualifying results may appear in tables (I5). The control group fits acceptable control populations (healthy participants) (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not non-empirical, measures PTSD specifically, reports a between-group contrast, and reports significant differences. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The NeuroStore record reports VBM (gray matter volume) analyses including a between-group VBM contrast of PTSD patients vs controls (Analysis 26441695_analysis_0: VBM between-group; gray matter volume) and an additional VBM between-group result reported with whole-brain correction (Analysis 26441695_analysis_4: VBM SDS−, corrected within whole brain, p<0.005, cluster extent 125, reported peaks). Participants include PTSD patients and healthy/trauma-exposed controls. Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. Thus the study is an empirical English MRI study of GM volume in PTSD (I3), provides whole-brain voxel-wise between-group VBM results (I4), allows use of reported coordinates/tables (I5), and uses acceptable control groups (I6). No exclusion criteria (only-ROI, non-empirical, non-PTSD, treatment/longitudinal only, only within-group, or only null results) are met. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the record.

This is an empirical, English-language voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing gray matter density between PTSD patients (rape victims) and control groups. The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (patients vs healthy controls and patients vs trauma-exposed without PTSD) with corrected inference and coordinate peaks reported in tables. Control groups include healthy and trauma-exposed without PTSD, which are acceptable. There is no indication the report is ROI-only, non-empirical, treatment/longitudinal-only, or null-only. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical structural MRI study reporting whole-brain voxel-wise results (GMV) within a sample of sexually assaulted women, it does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients versus controls. The NeuroStore record describes a within-group cross-subject regression (self-blame correlated with GMV) in the sexual-assault participant group (n=38) and no qualifying PTSD-vs-control GMV comparisons. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I3 and I4. Exclusion criterion E8 applies: the paper reports only within-group results in PTSD/trauma participants without a qualifying between-group contrast. Inclusion criteria met: none ([]) — the study does not provide the required PTSD vs control GMV comparison. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4.

This is an empirical VBM MRI study comparing PTSD patients (S) to trauma-exposed controls (NS) with a reported whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast (NS>S) and peak coordinates reported in tables. The analysis used whole-brain cluster-level correction and reported significant GM density differences. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume/density differences), I4 (whole-brain voxel-wise between-group PTSD vs controls), I5 (results reported as peak coordinates/tables), and I6 (controls are trauma-exposed/healthy). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes qualifying between-group contrasts).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI morphometry study comparing gray matter (GM) density between PTSD patients and non-PTSD controls (twin design). The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (non-PTSD > PTSD) with reported significant clusters (voxel-level and SVC-corrected results) and peak coordinates in tables, satisfying reporting requirements. Controls include trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD (acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, study is empirical, measures PTSD specifically, includes qualifying between-group contrasts, and reports significant differences. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical English-language MRI study that reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain between-group comparisons of gray matter volume between PTSD patients and healthy controls. The NeuroStore record specifies a whole-brain VBM contrast (healthy controls > PTSD patients), permutation testing fully corrected across space, and reported peak coordinates (26 peaks), satisfying availability of coordinate/table results. Controls are healthy individuals. The sample (n=50) and DSM-IV PTSD diagnosis are reported, and significant GM volume decreases in frontal and occipital lobes are documented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, measures PTSD vs controls between-group differences). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports comparisons within PTSD patients (dissociative subtype vs non-dissociative) and correlations within the PTSD sample, but does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (only within-group/subtype results and no qualifying PTSD vs control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no PTSD vs control GM volume comparison), I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise PTSD vs control contrast). The paper does report whole-brain VBM results and coordinates, but these are between PTSD subgroups and regressions, not comparisons against a control group, so it cannot be included in the PTSD vs control morphometry meta-analysis.

This is an empirical English VBM MRI study comparing GM volume in PTSD patients and controls (I3 met). Controls are non-traumatized coalminers (I6 met). Results are reported (tables/peaks) and qualifying results are available (I5 met). However, all reported between-group analyses are restricted to a hippocampus/amygdala mask with inference FDR-corrected within the ROI (spatial scope: region of interest). The paper does not report an unrestricted whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD vs controls, so it fails I4. Therefore E4 (ROI-only study with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies and the study must be excluded.

The study reports empirical structural MRI morphometry comparing PTSD patients and controls and includes at least one whole-brain between-group voxel-wise contrast (Analysis 30343133_analysis_0: TD > PTSD, whole-brain gray matter volume, cluster-corrected, reported peak coordinates). Results are available in tables (reported peaks), satisfying acceptable reporting formats. Controls are nontraumatized healthy youths. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, reports between-group whole-brain GM volume results (not ROI-only), and presents significant peaks (not only null results). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study includes PTSD patients and healthy controls and uses VBM, but it does not report a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls. The only whole-brain between-group contrast is a transdiagnostic patients (FEP, MDD, PTSD, OCD) > controls comparison; PTSD-specific results are reported only as ROI-based within-group/regression analyses. Therefore it fails to meet the requirement for a PTSD vs control whole-brain between-group contrast. Exclusion criterion E8 applies (only within-group PTSD results without a qualifying between-group contrast). Inclusion criterion I6 (acceptable control population: healthy controls) is satisfied. Inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are not met (no PTSD vs control GM volume between-group analysis; no PTSD whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast).

The paper reports only within-group structural MRI results (a correlation between P300 amplitude and anterior cingulate gray matter density in the PTSD group, n=6) and references a prior study for between-group reductions. It does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls comparing GM volume. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 and I4 and meets exclusion criterion E8 (only within-group results without a qualifying between-group contrast). The study does include trauma-exposed controls without PTSD (satisfies I6).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study comparing grey matter volumes in PTSD patients versus controls. The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts PTSD < HC and PTSD < TC with permutation-based FWE correction (TFCE) and reported coordinate peaks (tables), satisfying whole-brain reporting and allowing coordinate extraction. Control groups include both healthy and trauma-exposed controls. The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only reporting, not non-empirical, measures PTSD vs controls, includes qualifying between-group contrasts, and reports significant differences).

The study reports VBM structural analyses in bereaved adults but the NeuroStore extraction shows only within-group voxel-wise regression results in the PTSD subgroup (n=57). No whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls is reported. Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirement for studies assessing GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (reports only within-group results in PTSD patients without a qualifying between-group contrast). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no PTSD vs control GM volume differences reported), I4 (no whole-brain between-group PTSD vs control contrast). Full text is available for screening (no access issue).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of gray matter volume in combat-exposed veterans with and without PTSD. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses including a between-group contrast (Non-PTSD > PTSD) and voxel-wise regressions of CAPS scores against GMV, with significant peaks reported in tables. Controls are trauma-exposed non-PTSD patients, which fits acceptable control populations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, measures PTSD, includes between-group contrasts, reports significant differences). Thus it meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of morphometry studies of PTSD.

The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group morphometric contrasts comparing PTSD patients and healthy controls at baseline (Analyses 28287194_analysis_2 and _3), measuring gray matter volume with coordinates reported (tables of peaks) and cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo, p<0.01). Participants are drug-naïve PTSD patients vs healthy controls (n=37). Thus the study is an empirical structural MRI study of GM volume differences and provides whole-brain between-group results with coordinates available. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not non-empirical, PTSD was measured, and despite being a treatment study it includes qualifying between-group contrasts at baseline.

Empirical English-language structural MRI VBM study comparing PTSD patients (n=21-38 depending on analysis) with trauma-exposed controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected within whole brain, voxel-level) showing reduced hippocampus and rostral anterior cingulate in PTSD, and reports peaks/coordinates and a within-PTSD regression (duration vs hippocampal volume). Controls are trauma-exposed and results are reported (peaks). Thus it satisfies I3 (empirical MRI GM volume comparison), I4 (whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD vs controls), I5 (results/coordinates reported), and I6 (trauma-exposed controls). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is available in the provided record.

The study reports only within-group voxel-wise regressions of gray matter volume on PTSD symptom (flashback/reexperiencing) scores in a sample of 28 PTSD patients; no control group or between-group PTSD vs control GM volume comparisons are reported. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (only within-group results without a qualifying between-group contrast). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no MRI comparisons between PTSD patients and controls), I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise between-group PTSD vs control contrast), I5 (no qualifying between-group results reported even though coordinates are given for within-group effects), I6 (no control population present). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is an empirical structural MRI morphometry study of GM volume including PTSD patients and control groups (meets I3) and reports coordinate peaks in MNI (meets I5). Controls include trauma-exposed and nonexposed healthy subjects (meets I6). However, all reported analyses are marked as region-of-interest (ACC gyrus) rather than whole-brain voxel-wise contrasts; therefore the paper does not provide a qualifying whole-brain between-group GM-volume contrast (does NOT meet I4). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results). Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E4. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion IDs not met: I4.

The reported analysis is an ROI-based voxelwise comparison (spatial scope: region of interest; inference: corrected within ROI). Inclusion criterion I4 requires at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls; no whole-brain analyses are reported in the study document. The study does meet I3 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls) and I6 (control population acceptable), but because it reports only ROI results it falls under exclusion E4 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Reported peaks indicate non-null findings, so E9 does not apply.

This is an empirical structural MRI morphometry study comparing maltreated youth with PTSD, maltreated without PTSD, and non-maltreated controls (meets I3 and I6). However, the NeuroStore record shows analyses were region-of-interest (ROI)–masked voxel-based morphometry (e.g., orbitofrontal, amygdala, hippocampus, ACC mask) and the extracted analyses indicate ROI scope; there is no evidence of an unmasked whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast comparing PTSD patients vs controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only ROI analyses reported). Exclusion IDs met: E4. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I6. Inclusion IDs not met: I4. Full text appears complete in the record (no access notice).

This is an empirical English-language VBM study assessing gray matter volume with PTSD patients and healthy controls (I3). NeuroStore extracts show a between-group contrast comparing controls > PTSD (Analysis_21418787_analysis_0) with whole-brain spatial scope and reported peak coordinates in a table, satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast (I4). Results are reported as coordinates/tables (I5). Control group comprises healthy participants, which is acceptable (I6). Although the reported inference for the between-group contrast indicates small-volume correction within an ROI, the record indicates whole-brain spatial scope and reported peaks, and qualifying results are available in tables; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, within-group-only, treatment/longitudinal-only, null-only) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.
